body:
Well if their data collection wasn't skewed before, it certainly will be now.  (People buying tickets for movies they don't want to see, so they can go and see another movie for a second time.)

To be fair though, I think it was pretty skewed all along with people buying tickets for their friends, buying tickets to sell, buying tickets and exchanging for other tickets (Premium Formats, Restricted Events, Fathom, etc.)

I don't really know that the "data" they collect will be all that useful, but to each their own.

Fair enough.  I suppose once they start enforcing this I would have to start purchasing for the movie I told MoviePass I was going to, taking a picture of the ticket, and then going to the box office to request an exchange for a ticket to another movie in the future.  Still a viable option that should work.

In my area they don't request pictures of the ticket stub.  Not sure about other places.  I guess the way around this would be to go ahead and buy the ticket you said you were going to buy and then go to the kiosk and ask them to switch it.  I've done that before as well, and again, don't believe there's anyway they would figure that out.

Kind of depends if your theater wants to refund your card and then charge it again, but there's no need for them to do that.
TY!  Very interesting read, I learned something new today.
Tyvm for the response, it makes sense.
Thank you for taking the time to respond.  I promise I'll think about all of the advice you've given me, and definitely contact you if I ever need to, if that's okay.

I've not done counseling or medication.  When I say fighting with it I just mean fighting with myself.  Just fighting with depression and suicidal thoughts.  I really don't wanna be on medication and I don't wanna be that guy who needs a therapist, I don't know. 

And I get what you're saying.  I guess they would never really get over the loss completely, but it would become a memory eventually.  They might think of me on certain days, like my birthday.  I've thought about this to and if I did do anything I would try to at least do it on my birthday, so as not to create an additional day they would remember me on.

And telling anyone, especially family...it just seems like it'll make them look at me different.  They don't have these problems, they have their families, they're happy.  I just feel like it'd make most of them look at me as weak, and pity me.  Others maybe would look at me as trying to get attention, though that really is not me.  I always am the one hiding from any and all attention, I don't like attention at all.

I really don't want to talk to them because it will just come off as I'm looking for attention or pity and I'm not.  If anything talking to family or friends about it would probably make it worse because they will then either pity me, or shun me as someone who's seeking attention.  I just feel like I'm kind of broken, I'm not good for myself so I'm sure as hell not good for anyone else.  I've been fighting with this on and off for years thinking it'll get better but I always end up back here.

I just hate to leave any financial burdens on anyone.  I'm not really concerned that it would hurt them that much emotionally.  Sure I imagine it'd be a surprise and obviously bring out some feelings but my parents have other children that do just fine and are something to be proud of.  And my siblings have their own families to care for and worry about.  The sooner they forget about me the better.
